task: discrete visual vocabulary from frozen FetalCLIP patch features (IMPACT, 20413 frames, 12 of 24 layers)

flat_single_codebook.note: first run crashed on json int64 AFTER training and lost outputs; rerun with fix saved model+code maps

findings: Depth-factorised vocabulary reconstructs better than flat (0.298 vs 0.366) and no codebook collapses (all fully used).
Depth-specific content dominates: shared-only recon 0.830 (near the ~1.0 no-recon baseline) vs 0.298 full -> the depth-invariant part carries little; the per-depth deviations carry most.

GA is DIFFUSE, not depth-localised: max |code-freq vs GA| rho is 0.10-0.15 in EVERY vocabulary (shared and all three private). The weak GA structure is a property of FetalCLIP patch features, not of the flat architecture.
caveats: RECON COMPARISON NOT BIT-MATCHED: flat = 8 bits/patch (1-of-256); factorised = 25 bits/patch (1-of-128 + 3x 1-of-64). Part of the 0.366->0.298 improvement is extra discrete capacity, not factorisation per se. A bit-matched control is required before claiming factorisation itself wins.

SHARED-ONLY metric partly built in: shared = MEAN across groups while each group is the reconstruction target, so if groups differ the mean is inherently a poor predictor. The direction is real; the +0.53 effect size is inflated by the mean+residual construction.
EMA codebook + dead-code reinit were required: an earlier image-level VQ (gradient codebook, full-batch) collapsed to 9/32-12/64 codes with near-zero GA ladder and was NOT reported as a finding.
next_control: bit-matched factorised vs flat (e.g. shared K=32 + private K=8x3 ~= 14 bits vs flat K=16384 impractical -> match downward: flat K=64 (6 bits) vs shared K=16 + private K=4x3 (~10 bits), or equalise by shrinking private codebooks until total bits == flat bits)
